title: They told you everything is already forgiven.
paragraphs:
They told you everything is already forgiven.
Past. Present. Future.
So let me ask you something you don’t say out loud—

Why do you still feel guilty…
for something no one else knows?

Why does your heart race when the lights go off…
and your thoughts get loud?
Because this isn’t just theology.
This is personal.
There’s a man in Scripture we don’t give enough attention to.

Not a prophet.
Not a pastor.
Not a “good person trying his best.”
A criminal.
Pinned to a cross beside Jesus Christ.

Bleeding.
Dying.
Guilty.

No excuses left.
No future to fix.
No time to rewrite his story.
And yet—this man does something shocking.

He looks at Jesus…
through blood, through pain, through shame…
and whispers:
“Jesus, remember me when You come into Your kingdom.” (Luke 23:42)
That’s it.

No polished prayer.
No religious résumé.
No promise to “do better.”
Just a broken man reaching for mercy.
And Jesus answers with words that still shake eternity:
“Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in paradise.” (Luke 23:43)
Today.

Not after a probation period.
Not after proving loyalty.
Not after cleaning up.
Today.
Let that sit in your chest for a second.

This man had a past full of sin.
A present filled with consequences.
And no future to offer God.
Yet Jesus gave him… everything.
Here’s the truth most people either water down—or weaponize:
The cross is enough.
When Jesus said:
“It is finished.” (John 19:30)
He didn’t mean, “I’ve started something you need to complete.”
He meant the debt of sin—fully paid.

Past sin.
Present sin.
Even the sins you haven’t committed yet.
Covered.
But don’t twist it.
Because grace is not permission to stay in darkness.
It’s power to step into light.
Some scholars explain it this way:

When you are truly united with Christ by faith,
His once-for-all sacrifice (Hebrews 10:10)
covers the full penalty of your sin.

Not partially.
Not temporarily.
Fully.
But Scripture also refuses to let us play games with that truth.
“Repent… and turn to God, so that your sins may be wiped out.” (Acts 3:19)
“No one who lives in Him keeps on sinning…” (1 John 3:6)
So what gives?
Here’s the tension—and the beauty:
You are not saved by your transformation.
You are saved for transformation.
Look again at the thief.
In one moment—

His heart shifted.
His pride broke.
His eyes opened.
That’s repentance.
Not perfection overnight.
But direction—toward Jesus.
He didn’t climb down from the cross and start a new life.
But if he had?
He wouldn’t go back to the old one.

Because when grace hits you for real—
it doesn’t make you casual about sin.
It makes you hate what once owned you.
So let’s make it plain.
If you’re in Christ—

Your past is not chasing you anymore.
Your present is not disqualifying you.
Your future is not uncertain.
Because Jesus already stepped into all three.

But if you’re using “forgiven” as a cover…
to keep doing what you know breaks God’s heart—
That’s not freedom.
That’s deception.
And God loves you too much to leave you there.
This message is not here to shame you.
It’s here to wake you up.
Because the same Jesus who said “today” to a dying criminal…
is speaking to you right now.

Not when you fix everything.
Not when you feel worthy.
Now.
So what do you do?
You stop hiding.
You stop pretending.
You stop negotiating with sin like it’s harmless.
And you do what that man did—

You turn your head…
you fix your eyes on Jesus…
and you say:
“Remember me.”
And here’s the Gospel—clear and unshaken:
He will.

Not because you earned it.
Not because you cleaned yourself first.
But because He already paid for it.
In full.
This is your moment.

Not yesterday.
Not someday.
Today.
Turn.
Receive grace.
Walk free.

Someone out there is silently carrying shame
that Jesus already died to remove.

Pray for them.
Be the voice that reminds them—
It is finished.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
